verdicts.clause: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction
verdicts.reasoning: The rendered items ask the student to solve word problems involving sequential additions and subtractions of items (eggs, money, marbles, stickers, notebooks).
Each sampled word problem presents 3 to 4 sequential numbers to add or subtract. For instance, seed 11 gives 60, 58, 66, 76 (4 numbers), while seed 42 gives 36, 32, 29 (3 numbers).
All the numbers used in the word problems (like 76, 80, 59, 4) have at most 2 digits, fitting the constraint of up to 2 digits.
Several samples explicitly involve money, denoted by the Philippine peso sign (₱), such as 'Fidel starts with ₱36' in seed 42 or 'Carlo starts with ₱78' in seed 57.
